groups.translation: At that time, as they were returning, the boy Jesus remained in Jerusalem, and His parents did not know it. Supposing that He was in the company, they went a day’s journey and sought Him among their kinsfolk and acquaintances. And not finding Him, they returned to Jerusalem, seeking Him. And it came to pass that after three days they found Him in the temple, sitting in the midst of the teachers, listening to them and asking them questions. And all who heard Him were amazed at His wisdom and His answers. And when they saw Him, they wondered. And His Mother said to Him: Son, why have You done this to us? Behold, Your father and I have been seeking You in sorrow. And He said to them: Why is it that you were seeking Me? Did you not know that I must be in the things that are My Father’s? And they did not understand the word that He spoke to them. And He went down with them and came to Nazareth, and was subject to them.

Elizabeth’s time to give birth had come, and she bore a son. And her neighbors and kinsfolk heard that the Lord had shown His great mercy toward her, and they rejoiced with her. And it came to pass that on the eighth day they came to circumcise the child, and they were calling him by his father’s name, Zechariah. But his mother answered and said: Not so; he will be called John. And they said to her: There is no one among your kindred who is called by this name. And they were making signs to his father, asking what he wished him to be called. And asking for a writing tablet, he wrote, saying: John is his name. And they all marveled. And at once his mouth was opened and his tongue loosed, and he spoke, blessing God. And fear came upon all their neighbors; and all these things were being reported throughout all the hill country of Judea. And all who had heard them laid them up in their heart, saying: What, do you think, will this child be? For indeed the hand of the Lord was with him. And Zechariah his father was filled with the Holy Spirit and prophesied, saying: Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, because He has visited and brought about the redemption of His people.

Brethren: I give thanks to God, who has put the same earnest care for you into the heart of Titus; for he indeed accepted the appeal, but being more earnest, he set out to you of his own will. We have also sent with him the brother whose praise is in the Gospel throughout all the churches; and not only that, but he was also appointed by the churches as the companion of our journey in this grace, which is administered by us for the glory of the Lord and for our resolved will: avoiding this, lest anyone should find fault with us in this abundance which is administered by us. For we take thought for what is good, not only before God, but also before men. Show them, therefore, before the face of the churches, the proof of your love and of our glory on your behalf.

At that time, the Lord appointed also seventy-two others, and He sent them two by two before His face into every city and place to which He Himself was about to come. And He was saying to them: The harvest indeed is great, but the laborers are few. Ask the Lord of the harvest, therefore, to send out laborers into His harvest. Go: behold, I send you like lambs among wolves. Carry neither purse, nor bag, nor shoes, and greet no one on the way. Whatever house you enter, first say: Peace to this house; and if a son of peace is there, your peace will rest upon him; but if not, it will return to you. And remain in the same house, eating and drinking what they have; for the laborer is worthy of his wages. Do not pass from house to house. And whatever city you enter and they receive you, eat what is set before you; and cure the sick who are there, and say to them: The kingdom of God has come near to you.

At that time, Jesus saw a man sitting at the tax office, Matthew by name. And He said to him: Follow me. And rising, he followed Him. And it came to pass, as He was sitting at table in the house, behold, many publicans and sinners came and were sitting at table with Jesus and His disciples. But Jesus, hearing it, said: Those who are well have no need of a physician, but those who are ill. Go, then, and learn what this means: It is mercy I desire, and not sacrifice. For I did not come to call the just, but sinners.

In those days, Peter, standing up among the brethren — now there was a crowd of people together, about one hundred twenty — said: Men, brethren, it is necessary that the Scripture be fulfilled which was spoken beforehand by the Holy Spirit through the mouth of David about Judas, who was the leader of those who seized Jesus; who had been counted among us, and received the lot of this ministry. And this man indeed possessed a field from the reward of iniquity, and, having been hanged, burst open in the middle, and all his entrails were poured out. And this became known to all who lived in Jerusalem, so that that field was called in their tongue Aceldama, which means, the field of blood. In the book of Psalms, indeed, it is written: Let their abode become deserted, and let there be no one to dwell in it; and let another take his bishopric. It is necessary, then, that from these men who have assembled with us all the time in which the Lord Jesus went in and out among us, beginning from the baptism of John until the day on which He was taken up from us, one of these become with us a witness of His resurrection. So they proposed two: Joseph, who was called Barsabas, who bore the surname Justus, and Matthias. And praying, they said: Lord, You who know every heart, make known which one You have chosen of these two to receive the place of this ministry and of the apostleship, from which Judas turned aside through transgression, to depart to his own place. Then they gave them lots, and the lot fell on Matthias, and he was counted with the eleven apostles.

And no one knows the Son but the Father, nor does anyone know the Father but the Son, and he to whom the Son wills to reveal Him. In those days, King Herod laid hands on some members of the church to afflict them. And he killed John’s brother James with the sword. And when he saw that it was pleasing to the Jews, he went on to arrest Peter as well. Now it was during the days of Unleavened Bread. When he had arrested him, he sent him into prison, delivering him to four detachments of four soldiers to guard him, meaning to present him after the Passover to the people. Peter indeed was kept in prison. But prayer for him was being offered to God by the church without ceasing. Now when Herod was going to bring him out, that same night Peter was asleep between two soldiers, bound by two chains, and guards before the door were guarding the prison. And behold, there stood an angel of the Lord, and a light flashed in the room; and striking Peter’s side, he roused him, saying: Get up quickly. And the chains dropped from his hands. The angel then said to him: Fasten your belt, and tie your sandals on. And he did so. Then he told him: Wrap yourself in your garment, and follow me. And he went out and was following him, and he was unaware that what was happening through the angel was real, but he supposed he saw a vision. Then, passing the first guard and the second, they reached the iron gate leading to the city, which was opened for them of itself. And going out, they passed along one street, and at once the angel left him. And Peter, returning to himself, said: I know now for certain that the Lord sent His angel and rescued me from Herod’s hand and from every expectation of the Jewish people.

And when he saw that it was pleasing to the Jews, he went on to arrest Peter as well. Now it was during the days of Unleavened Bread. When he had arrested him, he sent him into prison, delivering him to four detachments of four soldiers to guard him, meaning to present him after the Passover to the people. Peter indeed was kept in prison. But prayer for him was being offered to God by the church without ceasing. Now when Herod was going to bring him out, that same night Peter was asleep between two soldiers, bound by two chains, and guards before the door were guarding the prison. And behold, there stood an angel of the Lord, and a light flashed in the room; and striking Peter’s side, he roused him, saying: Get up quickly. And the chains dropped from his hands. The angel then said to him: Fasten your belt, and tie your sandals on. And he did so. Then he told him: Wrap yourself in your garment, and follow me. And he went out and was following him, and he was unaware that what was happening through the angel was real, but he supposed he saw a vision. Then, passing the first guard and the second, they reached the iron gate leading to the city, which was opened for them of itself. And going out, they passed along one street, and at once the angel left him. And Peter, returning to himself, said: I know now for certain that the Lord sent His angel and rescued me from Herod’s hand and from every expectation of the Jewish people.

At that time, Jesus said to His disciples: Let your heart not be troubled. You believe in God; believe in Me as well. In the house of My Father there are many dwellings. Thomas says to Him: Lord, we do not know where You go, and how can we know the way? Jesus says to him: I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father other than through Me. If you had known Me, you would certainly have known My Father as well; and from now on you will know Him, and you have seen Him. Philip says to Him: Lord, show us the Father, and it is enough for us. Jesus says to him: I have been with you so long, and you have not come to know Me? Philip, whoever sees Me sees the Father as well. How is it that you say: Show us the Father? Do you not believe that I am in the Father, and the Father in Me? The words that I speak to you, I do not speak from Myself. But the Father who remains in Me, He Himself does the works. Do you not believe that I am in the Father, and the Father in Me? Otherwise, believe on account of the works themselves. Amen, amen, I say to you: whoever believes in Me, he too will do the works I do, and he will do greater things than these, for I go to the Father. And whatever you ask of the Father in My name, this I will do.

At that time, Jesus said to His disciples: These things I command you, that you love one another. If the world hates you, know that it has hated Me before you. If you had been of the world, the world would love its own; but because you are not of the world, but I have chosen you out of the world, therefore the world hates you. Remember My word that I said to you: A servant is not greater than his master. If they have persecuted Me, they will also persecute you; if they have kept My word, they will also keep yours. If I had not come and spoken to them, they would have no sin; but now they have no excuse for their sin. Whoever hates Me hates My Father also. If I had not done among them the works that no one else has done, they would have no sin; but now they have both seen and hated both Me and My Father. But that the word may be fulfilled which is written in their law: They have hated Me without cause.

Behold, he comes, leaping upon the mountains, bounding over the hills. My beloved is like a roe and a young deer. See, he himself stands behind our wall, looking in through the windows, looking out through the lattices. See, my beloved speaks to me: Arise, make haste, my love, my dove, my beautiful one, and come. For the winter has now passed; the rain has gone away and withdrawn. Flowers have appeared in our land; the season of pruning has arrived; the voice of the turtledove has been heard in our land; the fig tree has brought forth its green figs; the vines in blossom have yielded their fragrance. Arise, my love, my fair one, and come. My dove in the holes in the rock, in the hollow of the wall, show me your face, let your voice sound in my ears; for your voice is sweet, and your face is comely.

At that time, Mary, rising up, went into the hill country with haste, into a city of Judah; and she went into the house of Zechariah and greeted Elizabeth. And it came to pass that when Elizabeth heard the greeting of Mary, the infant leaped in her womb; and Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit, and she exclaimed in a loud voice and said: Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb. And how has this fallen to me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me? For behold, as soon as the voice of your greeting sounded in my ears, the infant in my womb leaped with joy. And blessed are you who have believed, because the things that were spoken to you by the Lord will be fulfilled. And Mary said: My soul magnifies the Lord, and my spirit has rejoiced in God my Savior.
